Oracle essential root causes/evidence vs. diagnosis:

Root cause 1 (dispatch/subsampling bug): GRPOTrainer._generate_single_turn uses self.num_generations=4 for post-tool continuations; VLLMGeneration.generate assumes repeated identical prompts, subsamples all_prompts[::num_generations], requests n=num_generations per retained prompt; after tool calls histories diverge so continuations get assigned to rows whose histories were never sent. Counted false: the diagnosis instead blames reward sparsity/optimization and never mentions GRPOTrainer/VLLMGeneration, subsampling, or mis-assigned histories.

Evidence 1 (request trace mismatches): 0/160 initial mismatches; 338/844 continuation mismatches. False: diagnosis does not mention request_traces.jsonl nor these mismatch counts.
Evidence 2 (group instance impact): 159/219 groups affected; 337/615 mismatching rows within divergent groups. False: not mentioned.
Evidence 3 (tool_traces.jsonl workspace identity linkage): False: diagnosis mentions tool-trace grades but not workspace identity/correspondence evidence.
Evidence 4 (metrics.jsonl shows nonzero training repair rewards and nonzero gradient on at least one update; dev reward 0.25 at steps 0-3; flat accuracy not evidence): Partly true only for the dev reward flatness — diagnosis says "dev split has 4 cases, eval reward stays at 0.25" (counts as mentioning dev reward 0.25 flat). It incorrectly asserts "grad_norm" is 0 and frames flatness as evidence for root cause.
Evidence 5 (weight_sync.jsonl completed updates; log-prob discrepancies are symptoms of wrong context): False: diagnosis cites weight_sync as unchanged weights but not the oracle’s point about completed updates or log-prob discrepancy symptom.

Counted-true quotes: "Unhealthy." and "the dev split has 4 cases, eval reward stays at 0.25".
Missing/wrong: it does not identify the oracle’s single framework root cause (post-tool continuation dispatch/subsampling leading to wrong histories) and omits the concrete request-trace mismatch evidence tying that mechanism to the run.
